All games Player props

Nothing here is staked, and nothing has a record against Kalshi yet. Each rung shows the model's chance next to what Kalshi charges for it. A rung is marked value only when one side is at least 7% cheaper than the model's price after Kalshi's fee, with the model between 20% and 80% and within 15 points of Kalshi's own price (a bigger disagreement usually means the market knows something the model doesn't). Every rung is logged and graded, and the record below fills in as games finish.

A player who doesn't play records nothing, so his overs lose. Probabilities are cut by the injury report: Questionable plays about 80% of the time here, Doubtful 25%.

What the backtest found

Walk-forward, 2019-2025: every season projected by models trained only on the seasons before it. There's no free archive of past prop prices, so this scores the model against what happened, not against the market. "Line" here is the player's own trailing average, a crude opener. Books set lines with far more than that, so these rates flatter the model. They show it's competent, not that it has an edge.

MarketError vs trailing avgConfident side hit"Always under"
Passing yards 60.81 vs 66.49 72.5% n=976 44.8%
Rushing yards 18.29 vs 18.55 66.9% n=4187 60.4%
Receiving yards 18.17 vs 18.53 66.0% n=6506 61.8%
Receptions 1.39 vs 1.42 69.1% n=4090 57.9%
Anytime TD log loss 0.4753 vs 0.5166——

The "always under" column is the reason to read the middle one carefully. Yardage averages sit above medians, so a line at the average goes under most of the time. A model has to beat that, not 50%.
